frontier.hypothesis: G1 - a spelling of 'two distinct variable index expressions on D_80099D3C' exists whose second index does not force a sixth callee-saved register, closing the last 3 instructions.
frontier.mechanism: F2 already reaches target's exact frame (vars=8) but reports regs=6/0 against target's 5/0; the extra sw/lw pair plus one reshuffled instruction is the entire remaining delta. The frame total is insensitive to the save count (compute_frame_size rounds gp_reg_size to 8), so the fix cannot lose the slot - only the instruction stream is at risk.
frontier.next_probe: Start from memory/grind/func_80049A2C/s8_variant_F2_frame48.c and sweep: (a) subscript the SECOND rotation read instead of the first, with src walking from kidx and the subscript at kidx+1; (b) derive the second index from arg1 directly (target keeps arg1 in $s1 across the whole body, so `(arg1 & 1) * 6` is recomputable without a new long-lived pseudo); (c) subscript the FINAL `new_var2` read with an index expression CSE cannot equate to `src + 2` (variants E and F5 died precisely because CSE rewrote them as `src[1]`). Measure each with tmp/grind/func_80049A2C/s8/batch.sh (reports .frame + insn count in one WSL call) and score the survivors through the sandbox.

frontier.hypothesis: G2 - the cheapest carrier is a semantically real SECOND index into D_800EF980 or D_80099CC8, whose symbol registers target already materialises.
frontier.mechanism: Target emits `lui/addiu %lo(D_80099CC8)` at 80049A34 and `lui/addiu %lo(D_800EF980)` at 80049A68, so those symbol registers exist in target's codegen at no extra cost; an address add off one of them is the cheapest possible orphan carrier. The function currently touches each symbol at exactly one index, which is why the s8 trigger law does not fire on them.
frontier.next_probe: Read the callers of func_80049A2C and the sibling writers of D_800EF980 (func_800493E4 writes it at two indices - temp_v1 and D_80099CC9[idx]) to determine whether this function semantically touches a second slot, e.g. the paired D_80099CC9 entry that func_800493E4 uses. If a real second index exists, it is an ordinary statement and the natural carrier; if the callers show it does not, bank G2 as dead.

frontier.hypothesis: G3 - the alternative decomposition vars=0 / args=24 remains formally open and almost certainly dead.
frontier.mechanism: current_function_outgoing_args_size is written only in calls.c (1400 / 2400 / 2750) from a call's own argument size; any 5th argument word is STORED at 0x10($sp) and target has zero non-save sp traffic. Bumping it without a store requires expanding a call and then deleting it, which is dead code.
frontier.next_probe: None recommended before G1 and G2 are spent. If revisited, look for a back-end-emitted library call (64-bit shift/divide) whose argument block is >= 20 bytes and whose insns are later eliminated.

judge_constraints: Grind must retire dummy[2], new_var4, the empty `if (a1_val) { }`, and the inline-assign `(new_var = new_var3)` — reach the same target bytes with pure C where every local has a semantic role and no un-annotated dead-store/dead-declaration constructs remain; if any construct proves genuinely unavoidable it must land as a documented FAKE carve-out with full lever-exhaustion evidence in the ledger and layer-2 review.

To close via the OVERSIZED-LOCALS carve-out fully-dead-pad case: first wire the prerequisite-aware `find_unused_local_arrays` allowlist through the engine (annotation-recognizing, engine test green) so the pad can stand WITHOUT a `(void) _pad;` shim; drop the void-cast reference in the candidate; and fix the annotation's frame arithmetic (5 saves = 20 bytes + 4 alignment pad, not `24 gp-saves`). Alternatively, keep grinding for a lever that eliminates the pad entirely (H4 cc1 -da instrumentation on the working baseline is still open in state.json.frontier).
